# AGENTS.md — Project Rules

Entry point for any agent working in this repo. Read this file first.

## Project
- Product name: `noAir` (GitHub repo: `noair-movie-downloader`)
- One-line purpose: Self-hosted web app that searches movies/TV via TMDB, finds torrent/magnet sources via Prowlarr, downloads them with qBittorrent (Docker), shows live download progress, and streams the video in-browser.
- Full plan lives in `docs/plan/00-index.md`.

## Commands
- Install deps: `cd backend && npm install` · `cd frontend && npm install`
- Run app: `docker compose up -d --build` (or `npm run dev` in `backend/` and `frontend/`)
- Test: `cd backend && npm test` · `cd frontend && npm test`
- Lint: `npm run lint` (each package)
- Typecheck: `npm run typecheck` (each package)

## Conventions
- TypeScript strict in both packages. Tests are Vitest (backend) with mocked external providers.
- API field names are camelCase; DB columns snake_case (see `docs/plan/02-specs.md` §5).
- External providers (TMDB, Prowlarr, qBittorrent) are always behind an interface in `backend/src/services/`.
- Secrets live only in `.env` (gitignored). Never commit keys. The TMDB key must never reach the browser — images go through `/api/images/tmdb/*`; portrait posters are downloaded once by the backend to the `art` volume and served from `/api/images/art/*` (D21).
- Credentials setup is documented in `docs/credentials.md` (template) and `docs/credentials.local.md` (gitignored local notes).
- qBittorrent is polled at exactly 2s intervals; never faster.

## Editing rules
- Design decisions belong in `docs/plan/00-index.md` — never invent them in code.
- Keep `docs/plan/` up to date when a design or spec changes; you are allowed (and expected) to edit these files when necessary.
- Follow the execution protocol in `docs/plan/00-index.md`.

## Do not touch
- `.env` (user secrets)

1: # Plan — Master Index & Doc Architecture
2: 
3: This document defines **how this planning set is structured** and how it will be executed. It is the entry point for any human or agent reading this repo.
4: 
5: ## Project
6: 
7: - **Name:** `noAir` (GitHub repo `noair-movie-downloader`)
8: - **One-line purpose:** Self-hosted web app that searches movies/TV via TMDB, finds torrent/magnet sources via Prowlarr, downloads them with qBittorrent (Docker), shows live download progress, and plays the finished video in-browser (or hands it to the user's local player).
9: 
10: ## Goal of this doc set
11: 
12: Produce a complete, unambiguous blueprint so that:
13: 
14: - A human can review the entire plan in under 15 minutes.
15: - An agent can execute the whole build top-to-bottom **without making design decisions**.
16: - Every task has a verifiable "done" condition.
17: 
18: ## Doc layout
19: 
20: ```
21: AGENTS.md                        # Project rules, commands, conventions — always read first
22: docs/plan/
23:   00-index.md                    # THIS FILE — overview, build order, locked decisions
24:   01-architecture.md             # System design: components, data flow, boundaries
25:   02-specs.md                    # Concrete contracts: API, data model, UI, providers
26:   03-tasks.md                    # Ordered, numbered milestones w/ acceptance criteria
27: ```
28: 
29: ## What each doc is FOR (and what it is NOT for)
30: 
31: | File | Contains | Must NOT contain |
32: |------|----------|------------------|
33: | `AGENTS.md` | Repo-level rules, run commands, edit conventions, pointer to this index | Project design decisions |
34: | `00-index.md` | Scope, goals, **locked decisions**, build order, conventions for the docs themselves | Implementation detail |
35: | `01-architecture.md` | Components, responsibilities, data flow diagrams, tech boundaries, what talks to what | Line-by-line implementation |
36: | `02-specs.md` | Concrete contracts: endpoints + payloads, schema, UI screens/flows, provider interfaces | Rationale, alternatives, opinions |
37: | `03-tasks.md` | Numbered tasks in build order; each with inputs, outputs, acceptance criteria | Design discussion |
38: 
39: ## Rules for writing every doc
40: 
41: 1. **Decisions, not options.** Every "we could use X or Y" becomes "we use X." No open choices left for the executor.
42: 2. **Requirements + acceptance criteria, not prose.** Facts an agent can verify. No ambiguous adjectives.
43: 3. **One fact lives in one place.** If two docs disagree, the doc that "owns" it wins (ownership table below). Cross-reference instead of duplicating.
44: 4. **Precise naming.** All names are written exactly once in `02-specs.md` and reused verbatim everywhere else.
45: 5. **No "later"/"TBD" in a doc that the executor reads.** Anything unknown is recorded in this file under Open Questions, resolved, then moved into the relevant doc.
46: 
47: ## Ownership table (single source of truth)
48: 
49: | Topic | Owned by |
50: |-------|----------|
51: | Tech stack, scope, build order | `00-index.md` |
52: | Components and data flow | `01-architecture.md` |
53: | API contracts, data model, UI, provider behavior | `02-specs.md` |
54: | Milestones, task order, acceptance criteria | `03-tasks.md` |
55: 
56: ## Locked decisions
57: 
58: | # | Decision |
59: |---|----------|
60: | D1 | Backend: **Node.js + Express 4 + TypeScript**. Single-user app, no auth. |
61: | D2 | Frontend: **React 18 + Vite + TypeScript**, React Router, **Zustand** for client state, plain CSS (no UI framework). |
62: | D3 | Database: **PostgreSQL 16 as a Docker service** (named volume), `pg` driver, schema run on backend boot. |
63: | D4 | Torrent indexer: **Prowlarr (Docker)**. One normalized search API; trackers (TPB, 1337x, etc.) configured in Prowlarr, not in code. |
64: | D5 | Downloader: **qBittorrent (Docker)** via its Web API v2. Backend polls it every 2s. |
65: | D6 | Metadata + imagery: **TMDB API** (free key). All poster/backdrop images proxied by the backend so the key never reaches the browser. |
66: | D7 | Realtime UI updates: **Socket.IO**. Server pushes a full downloads snapshot every 2s. |
67: | D8 | Playback: **play only after the file is fully downloaded**. qBittorrent writes in-progress files as `x.mkv.!qb` and renames them when complete; the backend never lists or serves `.!qb` files, so `stream_file_path`/`streamable` appear only once a complete file exists (inside a season pack, individually-completed episodes unlock early). Completed files are served over HTTP **Range** (`/api/stream/:infoHash`) for external players and browser-safe direct playback; `lib/streamPlan.ts` still routes browser-unsupported audio (→ AAC remux) and sub-4K HEVC (→ H.264 transcode) through ffmpeg for *completed* files, and 4K/UHD non-safe video to the external-player flow via the `movie://` scheme. Browser codec limits (H.264/VP9/AV1; no HEVC/.avi guarantee) still apply. `playinfo` also probes every audio/subtitle track for the browser-player upgrade. Packaging never re-encodes browser-safe AAC-LC audio (stream-copied) and runs renditions concurrently (S14); before packaging, Watch probes `mseProbe` codec strings and routes undecodable video (e.g. HEVC Main10) straight to the external-player screen. |
68: | D9 | Deployment: single `docker-compose.yml` with services `postgres`, `qbittorrent`, `prowlarr`, `backend`, `frontend`. Frontend served by nginx that proxies `/api` and `/socket.io` to the backend. |
69: | D10 | Cost: everything is free/open-source. Only required external account is a free TMDB API key; an **optional free OMDb key** (`OMDB_API_KEY`) enables portrait posters for the wide tiles (§4.6) — cards degrade to monograms when absent. |
70: | D11 | Testing: **Vitest** on the backend (unit tests with mocked providers); frontend smoke test via manual run in M4. |
71: | D12 | Magnet links: prefer Prowlarr-provided magnet; otherwise build from `infoHash` + 9 public trackers (list in `02-specs.md` §4.3). |
72: | D13 | LAN exposure: `frontend`, `qbittorrent` (Web UI), and `prowlarr` are all published on host ports (`0.0.0.0`). qBittorrent must have strong credentials (it has its own login); Prowlarr has no auth — documented risk accepted for a home LAN. `postgres` and `backend` stay internal-only. |
73: | D14 | TV browsing (v2): TV titles present TMDB **seasons/episodes**; contextual Prowlarr searches are whole-show (S3 no params), per-season (`?season=N` → season packs + episode releases), or per-episode (`?season=N&episode=M`). The Advanced picker retains the 30-row "Load more" + client-side filters/grouping from v1. **Friendly downloads auto-pick the most-seeded matching source**; releases with unparseable coverage are Advanced-only; a per-episode download never silently pulls a whole season. |
74: | D15 | Frontend visual language: **Netflix-style; black & white UI chrome over full-color artwork**. Left sidebar removed; fixed top header transparent at top that fades to a black gradient on scroll. Home = static cinematic brand hero + **16:9 full-bleed title-card tiles** (whole-card click, no captions/info icons) that bleed full-width with the rightmost card clipped to invite scroll; full-screen search overlay. Card art (superseded clause → **D21**): every tile is now the **OMDb-portrait composite** (no FanArt/TMDB imagery). Rail named "My Downloads"; **local-only playback resume** (C-DL2); **every friendly download opens a confirm sheet** naming the exact pick (C-DL1); **inline first-run guidance** (C-DL3). |
75: | D16 | TV metadata + episode columns: new `GET /api/media/:id/season/:n` (S12); `Source.coverage` from release titles with season gating on S3; downloads gain nullable `season_number`/`episode_number`/`backdrop_path` via idempotent `ALTER TABLE`; the file-list endpoint (S13) tags each file with season/episode server-side; `/watch/:infoHash?episode=SxxExx` auto-selects the matching file inside a season pack; the poll backfills season on legacy TV rows. |
76: | D17 | **~~Artwork pipeline v2 (poster-first tiles)~~ — SUPERSEDED by D21.** Kept for history: card identity is the poster, not the backdrop (Fanart/TMDB ladder, `art_files` cache, temporary `cardStyle` A/B). All of it (FanArt provider, enrichment, the Settings artwork controls) is **removed** by D21; only the `art_files` "poster on disk served via S8b" mechanism survived, re-sourced to OMDb. |
77: | D18 | **Hover-trailer previews — data layer**: every `TitleCard` resolves the title's best trailer for the hover card. Trailer metadata comes from TMDB `GET /movie/{id}/videos` / `GET /tv/{id}/videos` through the existing key — **no new key, no YouTube Data API, no backend storage** (`S15`). TV cards use the **series** trailer (per-episode trailers are not surfaced — TMDB coverage is sparse). The on-card presentation is **D20** (this entry no longer defines rendering). Embedding requires the *browser* to reach YouTube/Vimeo; the LAN box only needs TMDB reachability. |
78: | D19 | **Movie "the download is the loading screen" + version grouping**: the movie Detail hero renders one primary state (`DownloadsHeroPanel`) — no copy → Download best-match (inline "Best match · quality · size · seeds" hint, **Advanced**; shimmer while resolving) · copies arriving → status card (big tabular %, state, speed·ETA, Pause/Resume, Remove) · something playable → exactly one ▶ **Watch** (active version) + Player + delete with a **version-chip row** to switch, copies still downloading folded into mini-rows; **a disabled Watch is never rendered**. Best-source search runs only when the title owns no copy, is deduped + cached in the API client per context (~10 min), and lazily re-fetches after the last copy is deleted. Releases of one movie are **versions of a single library item** (`lib/versions.ts` pure helpers + `store/versionStore` persisted to `localStorage` keyed `movie:<tmdbId>`; default rule = most recently completed playable copy, tie-break higher resolution): My Downloads shows one card per movie with hover version chips; the Downloads page groups copies under `Movie · N versions` headers and labels each row `audio · quality`. Downloads persist `audioLang`/`audioMode` (idempotent `ALTER`, `S4`) so copies differing only by language stay distinguishable. TV keeps its episode layout and only reuses the panel for the active season pack; the C-DL1 confirm sheet is unchanged. |
79: | D20 | **Expanded Netflix-style hover card (replaces D18's inline overlay)**: every `TitleCard` expands into a **portaled, fixed pop-up card** after a sustained ~600 ms hover — width **1.7×** the base card (viewport-clamped), **vertically centered on the base cell (grows equally above and below)** and horizontally centered so it **overflows the neighbouring cards on all four sides**, `z-index: 150`, 8 px radius + strong dark shadow; base card keeps its grid slot (no white ring/scale while open); any scroll/resize dismisses it. Split layout: **media top (16:9)** = autoplay-looped trailer with **sound ON by default** (Chrome silences unmuted autoplay until the user has clicked the app once) + circular mute/unmute button that **remounts the iframe** (clip restarts), title/logo bottom-left over a scrim; **details bottom (dark column)** = compact Netflix-matching panel (16 px gutters, ~1.35 line-height, medium-500 13 px text): row 1 = Play (white circle → primary Watch action when present, else Detail) + two **decorative no-op circles** (Add to List `+`, Rate thumbs-up) + More Info chevron; My-Downloads version chips sit on their **own row beneath the actions**; row 2 = monochrome age-badge (`certification`) · duration ("2h 15m") or season count ("N Seasons") · `HD` chip (all 1 px translucent outlines, ~11 px); row 3 = up to three genre tags joined by `•`. Typeface is self-hosted **Inter Variable** (proprietary **Netflix Sans** is never bundled) standing in for the Netflix look. Data arrives from **S16** (`GET /api/media/:id/hover`), one call returning trailer + genres + runtime + seasons + certification, cached client-side ~1 h; US rating comes from TMDB `release_dates`/`content_ratings`. Every card expands even with no trailer (still artwork stands in); no pop-up for reduced-motion, `tmdbId <= 0`, or a failed/failed payload (static card). |
80: | D21 | **Netflix-style wide tiles from OMDb portraits — the winning card-art source.** Research: no free API serves *wide* per-title studio art except TMDB backdrops/FanArt (Netflix title cards are proprietary; OMDb returns only a portrait `Poster`). Decision: **wide 16:9 tile composited in-app from the OMDb portrait** — crisp portrait figure at full tile height over its own blurred ground; used everywhere (rails, My Downloads, downloads page, search, Detail hero as blurred ground). Pipeline: TMDB external_ids `imdbId` → OMDb (`OMDB_API_KEY`, budgeted ~850 req/day) → Amazon portrait downloaded once to the `art` volume (`art_files`, kind `poster`) → served by S8b, which **warms on first miss**; `empty` rows cached 7 days; no poster → monogram (never TMDB/FanArt imagery). **FanArt.tv and the whole artwork-settings cluster are deleted** (provider toggle, per-size preference, `cardStyle` A/B, preview tester, `ART_GRID` spike, `FANART_API_KEY`, `media_art`); `/api/settings` is audio-only; Settings shows no artwork controls. S8 TMDB proxy remains only for TV episode stills. |
81: 
82: ## Build order (how 03-tasks.md is sequenced)
83: 
84: Every milestone must be independently runnable and verifiable before the next starts:
85: 
86: 1. Project scaffold (repo layout, tooling, config, docker-compose, CI if any).
87: 2. Core domain logic that has no external dependencies (unit-testable first).
88: 3. External integrations one at a time, each behind an interface (TMDB, Prowlarr, qBittorrent).
89: 4. API layer over the domain logic (REST + Socket.IO).
90: 5. UI layer.
91: 6. End-to-end wiring, polish, and verification.
92: 
93: ## Execution protocol
94: 
95: 1. Agent reads `AGENTS.md`, then this file, then `03-tasks.md`.
96: 2. Agent works through tasks **in order**. Each task names exactly which of the other docs to read.
97: 3. After each task, the agent reports what it did and how the acceptance criteria were verified.
98: 4. A human confirms each milestone before the next begins.
99: 
100: ## Open Questions
101: 
102: - `Q1` Which trackers to enable in Prowlarr → resolved at runtime by the user in Prowlarr UI; code must not depend on any specific tracker. (Resolved by design, see D4.)
103: - `Q2` Pause/resume + delete-files options → nice-to-have, scheduled in `03-tasks.md` T5.3.
104: 
105: ## Change log
106: 
107: | Date | Change |
108: |------|--------|
109: | 2026-09-06 (art source) | **Netflix-style wide tiles from OMDb portraits (D21, this change set)**: research confirmed no free API serves *wide* per-title studio art except TMDB/FanArt (Netflix's is proprietary); decision — build the wide 16:9 tile in-app from a **portrait one-sheet**. New OMDb pipeline: TMDB `imdbId` → OMDb (`OMDB_API_KEY`, budgeted ~850/day) → Amazon poster downloaded once to the `art` volume (`art_files`, kind `poster` only) → served by S8b, which **warms on first miss** so any newly-rendered title resolves fast. `TitleCard`/hero/download tiles now render one fixed look: crisp portrait over its own blurred ground; monogram on 404 (never TMDB/FanArt art). **FanArt.tv removed app-wide** (`FANART_API_KEY`, media-art enrichment `art` on items/detail/downloads, hover logos, `ART_GRID` spike) and the whole **artwork settings cluster deleted** (provider/size-preference/`cardStyle` A/B + preview tester; `/api/settings` is audio-only). Settings shows no artwork controls. DB: `media_art` table dropped from schema (stale columns ignored); env/docs/`.env.example`/compose updated; backend + frontend tests/lint/typecheck green. |
110: | 2026-09-06 (hover polish) | **Netflix-parity hover-card bottom panel (D20 visual pass)**: compact 16 px-gutter details column with a real action row — Play + decorative no-op **Add to List** (`+`) and **Rate** (thumbs-up) circles beside it, More Info chevron right; My-Downloads version chips moved to their own row under the actions (out of the action row). Typography fixed: the CSS named proprietary **Netflix Sans** but never loaded it, so cards silently fell back to the thin generic system font (the "ugly gap"); now self-hosted **Inter Variable** (`@fontsource-variable/inter`) with medium-500 ~13 px panel text, tight 1.35 line-height, 1 px translucent outline badges (cert `R`/`TV-MA`, `HD`) at ~11 px, and `•`-joined genre tags with balanced 6 px spacing instead of stretched flex gaps. Pure presentational change: no functional My List/Rating backend (buttons are no-op, `title` "coming soon"). Docs D20 description, specs, and hover-card tests updated. |
111: | 2026-09-01 | Created doc architecture and conventions. |

# Plan — Master Index & Doc Architecture

This document defines **how this planning set is structured** and how it will be executed. It is the entry point for any human or agent reading this repo.

## Project

- **Name:** `noAir` (GitHub repo `noair-movie-downloader`)
- **One-line purpose:** Self-hosted web app that searches movies/TV via TMDB, finds torrent/magnet sources via Prowlarr, downloads them with qBittorrent (Docker), shows live download progress, and plays the finished video in-browser (or hands it to the user's local player).

## Goal of this doc set

Produce a complete, unambiguous blueprint so that:

- A human can review the entire plan in under 15 minutes.
- An agent can execute the whole build top-to-bottom **without making design decisions**.
- Every task has a verifiable "done" condition.

## Doc layout

```
AGENTS.md                        # Project rules, commands, conventions — always read first
docs/plan/
  00-index.md                    # THIS FILE — overview, build order, locked decisions
  01-architecture.md             # System design: components, data flow, boundaries
  02-specs.md                    # Concrete contracts: API, data model, UI, providers
  03-tasks.md                    # Ordered, numbered milestones w/ acceptance criteria
```

## What each doc is FOR (and what it is NOT for)

| File | Contains | Must NOT contain |
|------|----------|------------------|
| `AGENTS.md` | Repo-level rules, run commands, edit conventions, pointer to this index | Project design decisions |
| `00-index.md` | Scope, goals, **locked decisions**, build order, conventions for the docs themselves | Implementation detail |
| `01-architecture.md` | Components, responsibilities, data flow diagrams, tech boundaries, what talks to what | Line-by-line implementation |
| `02-specs.md` | Concrete contracts: endpoints + payloads, schema, UI screens/flows, provider interfaces | Rationale, alternatives, opinions |
| `03-tasks.md` | Numbered tasks in build order; each with inputs, outputs, acceptance criteria | Design discussion |

## Rules for writing every doc

1. **Decisions, not options.** Every "we could use X or Y" becomes "we use X." No open choices left for the executor.
2. **Requirements + acceptance criteria, not prose.** Facts an agent can verify. No ambiguous adjectives.
3. **One fact lives in one place.** If two docs disagree, the doc that "owns" it wins (ownership table below). Cross-reference instead of duplicating.
4. **Precise naming.** All names are written exactly once in `02-specs.md` and reused verbatim everywhere else.
5. **No "later"/"TBD" in a doc that the executor reads.** Anything unknown is recorded in this file under Open Questions, resolved, then moved into the relevant doc.

## Ownership table (single source of truth)

| Topic | Owned by |
|-------|----------|
| Tech stack, scope, build order | `00-index.md` |
| Components and data flow | `01-architecture.md` |
| API contracts, data model, UI, provider behavior | `02-specs.md` |
| Milestones, task order, acceptance criteria | `03-tasks.md` |

## Locked decisions

| # | Decision |
|---|----------|
| D1 | Backend: **Node.js + Express 4 + TypeScript**. Single-user app, no auth. |
| D2 | Frontend: **React 18 + Vite + TypeScript**, React Router, **Zustand** for client state, plain CSS (no UI framework). |
| D3 | Database: **PostgreSQL 16 as a Docker service** (named volume), `pg` driver, schema run on backend boot. |
| D4 | Torrent indexer: **Prowlarr (Docker)**. One normalized search API; trackers (TPB, 1337x, etc.) configured in Prowlarr, not in code. |
| D5 | Downloader: **qBittorrent (Docker)** via its Web API v2. Backend polls it every 2s. |
| D6 | Metadata + imagery: **TMDB API** (free key). All poster/backdrop images proxied by the backend so the key never reaches the browser. |
| D7 | Realtime UI updates: **Socket.IO**. Server pushes a full downloads snapshot every 2s. |
| D8 | Playback: **play only after the file is fully downloaded**. qBittorrent writes in-progress files as `x.mkv.!qb` and renames them when complete; the backend never lists or serves `.!qb` files, so `stream_file_path`/`streamable` appear only once a complete file exists (inside a season pack, individually-completed episodes unlock early). Completed files are served over HTTP **Range** (`/api/stream/:infoHash`) for external players and browser-safe direct playback; `lib/streamPlan.ts` still routes browser-unsupported audio (→ AAC remux) and sub-4K HEVC (→ H.264 transcode) through ffmpeg for *completed* files, and 4K/UHD non-safe video to the external-player flow via the `movie://` scheme. Browser codec limits (H.264/VP9/AV1; no HEVC/.avi guarantee) still apply. `playinfo` also probes every audio/subtitle track for the browser-player upgrade. Packaging never re-encodes browser-safe AAC-LC audio (stream-copied) and runs renditions concurrently (S14); before packaging, Watch probes `mseProbe` codec strings and routes undecodable video (e.g. HEVC Main10) straight to the external-player screen. |
| D9 | Deployment: single `docker-compose.yml` with services `postgres`, `qbittorrent`, `prowlarr`, `backend`, `frontend`. Frontend served by nginx that proxies `/api` and `/socket.io` to the backend. |
| D10 | Cost: everything is free/open-source. Only required external account is a free TMDB API key; an **optional free OMDb key** (`OMDB_API_KEY`) enables portrait posters for the wide tiles (§4.6) — cards degrade to monograms when absent. |
| D11 | Testing: **Vitest** on the backend (unit tests with mocked providers); frontend smoke test via manual run in M4. |
| D12 | Magnet links: prefer Prowlarr-provided magnet; otherwise build from `infoHash` + 9 public trackers (list in `02-specs.md` §4.3). |
| D13 | LAN exposure: `frontend`, `qbittorrent` (Web UI), and `prowlarr` are all published on host ports (`0.0.0.0`). qBittorrent must have strong credentials (it has its own login); Prowlarr has no auth — documented risk accepted for a home LAN. `postgres` and `backend` stay internal-only. |
| D14 | TV browsing (v2): TV titles present TMDB **seasons/episodes**; contextual Prowlarr searches are whole-show (S3 no params), per-season (`?season=N` → season packs + episode releases), or per-episode (`?season=N&episode=M`). The Advanced picker retains the 30-row "Load more" + client-side filters/grouping from v1. **Friendly downloads auto-pick the most-seeded matching source**; releases with unparseable coverage are Advanced-only; a per-episode download never silently pulls a whole season. |
| D15 | Frontend visual language: **Netflix-style; black & white UI chrome over full-color artwork**. Left sidebar removed; fixed top header transparent at top that fades to a black gradient on scroll. Home = static cinematic brand hero + **16:9 full-bleed title-card tiles** (whole-card click, no captions/info icons) that bleed full-width with the rightmost card clipped to invite scroll; full-screen search overlay. Card art (superseded clause → **D21**): every tile is now the **OMDb-portrait composite** (no FanArt/TMDB imagery). Rail named "My Downloads"; **local-only playback resume** (C-DL2); **every friendly download opens a confirm sheet** naming the exact pick (C-DL1); **inline first-run guidance** (C-DL3). |
| D16 | TV metadata + episode columns: new `GET /api/media/:id/season/:n` (S12); `Source.coverage` from release titles with season gating on S3; downloads gain nullable `season_number`/`episode_number`/`backdrop_path` via idempotent `ALTER TABLE`; the file-list endpoint (S13) tags each file with season/episode server-side; `/watch/:infoHash?episode=SxxExx` auto-selects the matching file inside a season pack; the poll backfills season on legacy TV rows. |
| D17 | **~~Artwork pipeline v2 (poster-first tiles)~~ — SUPERSEDED by D21.** Kept for history: card identity is the poster, not the backdrop (Fanart/TMDB ladder, `art_files` cache, temporary `cardStyle` A/B). All of it (FanArt provider, enrichment, the Settings artwork controls) is **removed** by D21; only the `art_files` "poster on disk served via S8b" mechanism survived, re-sourced to OMDb. |
| D18 | **Hover-trailer previews — data layer**: every `TitleCard` resolves the title's best trailer for the hover card. Trailer metadata comes from TMDB `GET /movie/{id}/videos` / `GET /tv/{id}/videos` through the existing key — **no new key, no YouTube Data API, no backend storage** (`S15`). TV cards use the **series** trailer (per-episode trailers are not surfaced — TMDB coverage is sparse). The on-card presentation is **D20** (this entry no longer defines rendering). Embedding requires the *browser* to reach YouTube/Vimeo; the LAN box only needs TMDB reachability. |
| D19 | **Movie "the download is the loading screen" + version grouping**: the movie Detail hero renders one primary state (`DownloadsHeroPanel`) — no copy → Download best-match (inline "Best match · quality · size · seeds" hint, **Advanced**; shimmer while resolving) · copies arriving → status card (big tabular %, state, speed·ETA, Pause/Resume, Remove) · something playable → exactly one ▶ **Watch** (active version) + Player + delete with a **version-chip row** to switch, copies still downloading folded into mini-rows; **a disabled Watch is never rendered**. Best-source search runs only when the title owns no copy, is deduped + cached in the API client per context (~10 min), and lazily re-fetches after the last copy is deleted. Releases of one movie are **versions of a single library item** (`lib/versions.ts` pure helpers + `store/versionStore` persisted to `localStorage` keyed `movie:<tmdbId>`; default rule = most recently completed playable copy, tie-break higher resolution): My Downloads shows one card per movie with hover version chips; the Downloads page groups copies under `Movie · N versions` headers and labels each row `audio · quality`. Downloads persist `audioLang`/`audioMode` (idempotent `ALTER`, `S4`) so copies differing only by language stay distinguishable. TV keeps its episode layout and only reuses the panel for the active season pack; the C-DL1 confirm sheet is unchanged. |
| D20 | **Expanded Netflix-style hover card (replaces D18's inline overlay)**: every `TitleCard` expands into a **portaled, fixed pop-up card** after a sustained ~600 ms hover — width **1.7×** the base card (viewport-clamped), **vertically centered on the base cell (grows equally above and below)** and horizontally centered so it **overflows the neighbouring cards on all four sides**, `z-index: 150`, 8 px radius + strong dark shadow; base card keeps its grid slot (no white ring/scale while open); any scroll/resize dismisses it. Split layout: **media top (16:9)** = autoplay-looped trailer with **sound ON by default** (Chrome silences unmuted autoplay until the user has clicked the app once) + circular mute/unmute button that **remounts the iframe** (clip restarts), title/logo bottom-left over a scrim; **details bottom (dark column)** = compact Netflix-matching panel (16 px gutters, ~1.35 line-height, medium-500 13 px text): row 1 = Play (white circle → primary Watch action when present, else Detail) + two **decorative no-op circles** (Add to List `+`, Rate thumbs-up) + More Info chevron; My-Downloads version chips sit on their **own row beneath the actions**; row 2 = monochrome age-badge (`certification`) · duration ("2h 15m") or season count ("N Seasons") · `HD` chip (all 1 px translucent outlines, ~11 px); row 3 = up to three genre tags joined by `•`. Typeface is self-hosted **Inter Variable** (proprietary **Netflix Sans** is never bundled) standing in for the Netflix look. Data arrives from **S16** (`GET /api/media/:id/hover`), one call returning trailer + genres + runtime + seasons + certification, cached client-side ~1 h; US rating comes from TMDB `release_dates`/`content_ratings`. Every card expands even with no trailer (still artwork stands in); no pop-up for reduced-motion, `tmdbId <= 0`, or a failed/failed payload (static card). |

S8 TMDB proxy remains only for TV episode stills. |

## Build order (how 03-tasks.md is sequenced)

Every milestone must be independently runnable and verifiable before the next starts:

1. Project scaffold (repo layout, tooling, config, docker-compose, CI if any).
2. Core domain logic that has no external dependencies (unit-testable first).
3. External integrations one at a time, each behind an interface (TMDB, Prowlarr, qBittorrent).
4. API layer over the domain logic (REST + Socket.IO).
5. UI layer.
6. End-to-end wiring, polish, and verification.

## Execution protocol

1. Agent reads `AGENTS.md`, then this file, then `03-tasks.md`.
2. Agent works through tasks **in order**. Each task names exactly which of the other docs to read.
3. After each task, the agent reports what it did and how the acceptance criteria were verified.
4. A human confirms each milestone before the next begins.

- `Q1` Which trackers to enable in Prowlarr → resolved at runtime by the user in Prowlarr UI; code must not depend on any specific tracker. (Resolved by design, see D4.)
- `Q2` Pause/resume + delete-files options → nice-to-have, scheduled in `03-tasks.md` T5.3.

1: /**
2:  * OMDb webservice client (portrait posters only).
3:  *
4:  * OMDb returns a single portrait `Poster` URL per IMDb id — the input to the
5:  * in-app wide-card composite (D21). The free tier is capped at 1,000 requests
6:  * per day, so the client enforces a conservative in-memory daily budget and
7:  * never lets the warm loop wedge the key.
8:  *
9:  * Results are status-aware and never throw:
10:  * - `ok`    → usable poster URL
11:  * - `empty` → the title has no poster (or no IMDb record) — storable
12:  * - `error` → transient failure OR the daily budget is exhausted — NOT storable
13:  */
14: 
15: export type OmdbStatus = 'ok' | 'empty' | 'error';
16: 
17: export interface OmdbPosterResult {
18:   status: OmdbStatus;
19:   posterUrl: string | null;
20: }
21: 
22: export interface OmdbClient {
23:   /** Resolve the Amazon-hosted portrait poster URL for an IMDb id (`tt1234567`). */
24:   fetchPoster(imdbId: string): Promise<OmdbPosterResult>;
25: }
26: 
27: export interface OmdbClientConfig {
28:   apiKey: string;
29:   baseUrl?: string;
30:   /** Conservative slice of the 1,000/day free tier. Default 850. */
31:   dailyLimit?: number;
32:   fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
33:   now?: () => number;
34: }
35: 
36: const REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000;
37: 
38: function dayKey(nowMs: number): string {
39:   return new Date(nowMs).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
40: }
41: 
42: export function createOmdbClient(config: OmdbClientConfig): OmdbClient {
43:   const fetchImpl = config.fetchImpl ?? fetch;
44:   const base = (config.baseUrl ?? 'https://www.omdbapi.com').replace(/\/+$/, '');
45:   const dailyLimit = config.dailyLimit ?? 850;
46:   const nowMs = config.now ?? Date.now;
47: 
48:   let budgetDay = dayKey(nowMs());
49:   let budgetUsed = 0;
50: 
51:   function consumeBudget(): boolean {
52:     const today = dayKey(nowMs());
53:     if (today !== budgetDay) {
54:       budgetDay = today;
55:       budgetUsed = 0;
56:     }
57:     if (budgetUsed >= dailyLimit) return false;
58:     budgetUsed += 1;
59:     return true;
60:   }
61: 
62:   async function fetchPoster(imdbId: string): Promise<OmdbPosterResult> {
63:     if (!/^tt\d+$/.test(imdbId)) {
64:       return { status: 'empty', posterUrl: null };
65:     }
66:     if (!consumeBudget()) {
67:       console.warn('[omdb] daily poster budget exhausted — skipping');
68:       return { status: 'error', posterUrl: null };
69:     }
70:     const url = `${base}/?apikey=${encodeURIComponent(config.apiKey)}&i=${encodeURIComponent(imdbId)}&plot=short&r=json`;
71:     try {
72:       const res = await fetchImpl(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS) });
73:       if (!res.ok) {
74:         // 429/5xx — transient, must not be cached as "no poster".
75:         return { status: 'error', posterUrl: null };
76:       }
77:       const data = (await res.json()) as { Response?: string; Poster?: string; Error?: string };
78:       if (data.Response === 'False') {
79:         return { status: 'empty', posterUrl: null };
80:       }
81:       const poster = data.Poster ?? '';
82:       if (!poster || poster === 'N/A') {
83:         return { status: 'empty', posterUrl: null };
84:       }
85:       try {
86:         const parsed = new URL(poster);
87:         if (parsed.protocol !== 'https:') return { status: 'empty', posterUrl: null };
88:       } catch {
89:         return { status: 'empty', posterUrl: null };
90:       }
91:       return { status: 'ok', posterUrl: poster };
92:     } catch {
93:       return { status: 'error', posterUrl: null };
94:     }
95:   }
96: 
97:   return { fetchPoster };
98: }

251:- Settings: existing System/Configuration/About cards + **Audio language** card + **Local player** card — platform-aware (`detectOs`): choose VLC/MPV/MPC-HC/PotPlayer on Windows, VLC/MPV on Linux (localStorage hint, `readPlayerPreference`); download the matching installer/uninstaller — `.cmd` (PowerShell, registers `movie://` under HKCU) on Windows, `.sh` (writes `movie-open.sh` + a `x-scheme-handler/movie` `.desktop` entry, registers via `xdg-mime`, auto-detects installed player via `command -v`/snap/flatpak) on Linux. 258:- **ConfirmDownloadSheet (C-DL1):** every friendly download (movie / season / episode) first shows a sheet naming the exact pick — release title, resolution/source/codec, size, seeders, indexer — with `[Start]` and `[Advanced…]`. 260:- **Resume (C-DL2):** `store/playbackStore` persists `{infoHash, file, seconds}` to `localStorage` every ~5s of playback. On return to the same file the player offers `Resume from mm:ss` / `Restart`. Local only; no server round-trip. Recents are marked on play start.
276:- Images: `https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/{w500|w1280}/{path}` (proxied, S8).
284:- Auth-bruteforce guard: `web_ui_max_auth_fail_count` (default 5) triggers an IP ban for `web_ui_ban_duration` (default 3600s). A backend polling with wrong credentials self-bans its container IP — clear it by restarting the qBittorrent container.
315:  1. `infoHash` present → use a real `magnetUrl` if it starts with `magnet:`, else build a magnet from `infoHash` (§4.3 magnet builder).
332:- Quirks: category `5000` covers episodes; a TV source's `title` may be a season pack, a partial pack, or a single episode — the parser (§4.5) derives `coverage` so the UI can label it; `coverage: null` releases are shown in the Advanced picker only. Only indexers that expose `infoHash` in search results (e.g. YTS API) populate it; others rely on the `downloadUrl` proxy path above.
354:### 4.6 Portrait-poster pipeline (OMDb → local `art` volume) — D21
355:- Problem researched: no free API exposes *wide* per-title studio art except TMDB backdrops and FanArt.tv (Netflix's own title-card art is proprietary). Decision: **build the wide tile in-app from a legal portrait one-sheet**. Portrait source = **OMDb** (Amazon-hosted, keyed by IMDb id).
356:- Config: optional `OMDB_API_KEY` in `.env`. Absent → art disabled (cards/heroes show the monogram placeholder). Free tier is **1,000 requests/day**; `services/omdb.ts` enforces a conservative daily budget (~850) and treats a budget miss as a transient error, never as "no poster".
357:- Resolution chain (`lib/warmArt.ts` + image route, one time per title): TMDB `GET /{movie|tv}/{id}/external_ids` (`tmdb.imdbId`) → OMDb `GET /?apikey=…&i=tt…` → Amazon `Poster` URL → downloaded once to `ART_DIR` (`art_files`, kind `poster` only) → served by **S8b**.
358:- `art_files` stores only `poster`; `media_art`, Fanart.tv, TMDB art proxies are **not** card sources (the S8 TMDB proxy remains only for TV episode stills).
359:- Warm loop covers browse rails + downloads at boot and every `ART_WARM_INTERVAL_MS`; the S8b route additionally **warms on first miss** so a freshly-rendered title (search result, download row) resolves its own poster without waiting for the loop. Titles with no poster are recorded `empty` (7-day retry window) so OMDb is not re-asked.
360:- Enrichment removed: search/browse/detail/downloads payloads no longer carry an `art` object; the frontend renders exactly one composite tile from `/api/images/art/:mediaType/:tmdbId/poster` and falls back to a monogram on 404/error (never TMDB/FanArt imagery). Detail-hero uses the same portrait as a blurred full-bleed ground.

52:       if (record.tmdbId != null && record.mediaType != null) {

200: - `ART_DIR` is a named compose volume (like `/downloads`, `/packages`) mounted at the backend's configured `ART_DIR` (default `/art`). Files are named `{mediaType}_{tmdbId}_poster.{ext}`.
201: 
202: ## 3. UI / CLI
203: 
204: Visual language (D15 + D21): **strict black & white, Netflix-style**. Fixed top header 68px that is transparent at the top of the page and fades to a black gradient (then solid `#000`) on scroll. Layout is full-bleed (no centered max-width column); content gutters are `4%`. Cards are **wide 16:9 tiles built in-app from the OMDb portrait poster** (§4.6): the portrait is the crisp figure at full tile height over its own blurred ground — the only card art source; rails bleed to the viewport edge so the rightmost card is clipped mid-card to invite horizontal scroll; a sustained hover expands the card into the **D20 pop-up** (video/art top + details column). All colors are grayscale tokens (`--bg #000`, surfaces, `#fff/#e5e5e5/#b3b3b3/#808080`); state chips/progress/seeders map to luminance, never hue.
205: 
206: Routes: `/` (Home), `/media/:id?type=` (Detail), `/watch/:infoHash` (Player), `/downloads`, `/settings`.
207: 
208: ### Shell: AppHeader (replaces the sidebar)
209: - Fixed 68px, content padded `0 4%`; transparent at `scrollY≈0`, fades to `linear-gradient(#000, rgba(0,0,0,.6), transparent)` then solid `#000` while scrolling (rAF-throttled).
210: - Left: wordmark → `/`. Nav links: **Home · Downloads · Settings** (`NavLink`, 14px, `#e5e5e5`, active white).
211: - Right: backend connection dot, live download-count badge, search toggle (opens overlay), settings gear.
212: - Mobile: hamburger → bottom-sheet with the same links + search.
213: 
214: ### Screen: Home (`/`)
215: - Sections top→bottom: **Hero** (static brand GIF, grayscaled via CSS; fallback TMDB `w1280` backdrop → black gradient) → **My Downloads** (named so because resume positions are deferred, D15) → **Recently Viewed** → **Trending This Week** → **Best Movies** → **Best Series**.
216: - Rail card = `TitleCard` (16:9 landscape backdrop; **expanded pop-up card (D20)** on sustained hover; white progress bar when downloading).
217: - My Downloads sources `DownloadRecord` (progress + quality chip when known); Recently Viewed sources the recents store.
218: 
219: ### Screen: Search overlay (all pages)
220: - Trigger: header search icon. Fixed `#000` overlay, `role="dialog"`, focus trap, Esc/× closes, focus restored to trigger.
221: - Big input (debounced 300ms → S1), `All | Movies | TV` segmented control, landscape-card result grid.
222: - Empty: "No results for '<q>'".
223: - **Result selection**: activating a result (click/Enter) navigates to `/media/:id?type=…`; the overlay closes on any route change committed beneath it (so the destination is never hidden behind the full-screen layer). Closing resets query/results; no auto-save of the typed term into recent searches.
224: 
225: - **Expanded Netflix-style hover card (D20, on every `TitleCard`)**: any card in a rail, My Downloads, the landscape result grid, or the search overlay expands into a **portaled pop-up card** on a sustained hover (debounced ~600 ms). Trigger → `hoverCardFor(item)` (**S16**, in-memory cache keyed `tmdbId:mediaType`, ~1h TTL); the pop-up opens immediately with the still art and fills in as the payload resolves. Card never has a trailer usable (or the fetch failed, `trailer:null`, `tmdbId <= 0`, or `prefers-reduced-motion`) → static card, no pop-up, no layout shift, no toast. TV cards play the **series** trailer.
226:   - **Scale/position**: the pop-up is `position: fixed` (portal, `z-index: 150`, 8 px radius, strong dark shadow). Width = **1.7×** the base card (clamped to the viewport), **vertically centered on the base cell so it grows equally above and below**, horizontally centered so it **overflows the neighbours on both sides**; it is clamped to stay inside the viewport (below the 68px header). The base card keeps its grid slot (hover scale/ring removed while open). Any scroll/resize dismisses the pop-up.
227:   - **Media half (16:9)**: iframe autoplays the looping trailer with **sound ON by default** — YouTube `https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/{videoId}?autoplay=1&mute=0&controls=0&playsinline=1&loop=1&playlist={videoId}&modestbranding=1`, Vimeo `…?autoplay=1&muted=0&loop=1&controls=0`. Chrome still silences unmuted autoplay until the user has clicked the app once. A **circular mute/unmute button** sits bottom-right (remounts the iframe, restarting the clip); the title/logo sits bottom-left over a scrim. Iframe is `pointer-events:none`; clicking the media runs the Play action.
228:   - **Details half (solid `--bg-2` column, compact: `12px 16px 14px` padding, ~1.35 line-height)**: Row 1 — **Play** (white circle; runs the card's `primary` Watch action when present, else opens Detail), two **decorative no-op circles** — **Add to List** (`+`) and **Rate** (thumbs-up; no My List/rating backend yet, `title` says "coming soon") — then **More Info** (chevron → Detail) on the right. Version chips (My Downloads) render on their **own row directly under the actions** (not inline). Row 2 — monochrome age-badge (`certification`, 1px translucent-white outline, ~11px) · duration (`movie` `runtime` → "2h 15m") or seasons count ("N Seasons") · bordered `HD` chip (both ~11px, `1px 4px` padding). Row 3 — up to three genre tags joined by `•` with tight 6px spacing. All grayscale tokens; text is medium-weight (500) ~13px sans-serif — self-hosted **Inter Variable** (`@fontsource-variable/inter`) stands in for proprietary **Netflix Sans** (never bundled), tuned weights/sizes, never the thin generic system fallback.
229: 
230: ### Screen: Media Detail (`/media/:id`)
231: - Hero: `w1280` backdrop, title, meta row (year · genres · runtime · rating; TV adds "N Seasons"), overview, grayscale overlays.
232: - **Movie** — hero shows exactly one primary state (D19):
233:   - **no copy** → primary ▶ **Download** (friendly most-seeded S3 movie source) with an inline "Best match · quality · size · seeds" hint under the button; **Advanced** (`SourcePickerModal`); while the source fetch runs the CTA reads `Finding the best release…` (shimmer, never a dead button). The S3 fetch runs **only when no copy is owned yet** and is cached per title+audio (S3 api cache), so revisiting an owned title never re-asks Prowlarr; deleting the last copy lazily re-fetches and returns the hero to the offer state.
234:   - **copies exist** → a single status area (`DownloadsHeroPanel`): **anything playable** ⇒ one ▶ **Watch** button (targets the active version) + **Player** + delete, with a **version-chip row** to switch which ready copy is "the" copy; copies still downloading collapse into compact mini-rows. **Nothing playable yet** ⇒ a status card (big tabular %, state, speed · ETA, Pause/Resume, Remove) for the focused copy, plus chips to focus another when several are arriving. **No disabled Watch is ever rendered.**
235: - **TV**:
236:   - Season dropdown — default = season with an active download, else the lowest `seasonNumber` with `episodeCount > 0` (S2). Season change → one lazy `S3?season=N` search (cached per `title|season`, request-id guarded, skeleton rows) + `S12` episodes.
237:   - Episode rows: still thumb (`w500`), big episode number, title, runtime, overview, availability chip; hover highlight.
238:     - **Friendly download** (`ArrowDownToLine`): most-seeded source whose `coverage` covers the episode — exact single-episode releases preferred; a partial pack is allowed and labeled `E0X–E0Y`; **never** auto-downloads a whole season. No exact source → info toast + Advanced pre-scoped `season=N&episode=M`.
239:     - Episode inside an active full-season download → **Play** (→ `/watch/:hash?episode=SxxExx`) instead of download.
240:   - Season header: **Download season** → most-seeded full-season pack (`coverage … episodes === null`); if active → progress + Watch + trash.
241:   - **Advanced** (`SlidersHorizontal`): `SourcePickerModal` listing **all** Prowlarr results for the current season/episode scope, including `coverage: null` releases (never auto-picked; shown with their release title). Reuses v1 structured filters (resolution/source/codec/indexer/min-seeders/size/regex), sort, cross-indexer grouping + "Show duplicates", count line, and 30-row "Load more".
242: - Actions (both types): friendly/advanced download → `POST S4`; `201` toast "Added to downloads"; `409` toast "Already downloading". Trash → confirm → `DELETE S6?deleteFiles=true`.
243: 
244: ### Screen: Player (`/watch/:infoHash`[`?episode=SxxExx`])
245: - Optional `?episode=SxxExx` (TV, season-pack downloads): after the S13 file list loads, auto-select the first file whose server-parsed `seasonNumber`/`episodeNumber` matches; no match → normal file-picker state.
246: - Playback is gated on completion (D8): a torrent that has no fully-downloaded video yet shows a *waiting* state with download % that reloads automatically once `streamable` flips true. `S7b` mode decision; `direct`/`remux-audio`/`transcode` `<video>`; `player-required` → "Open in your player" (`movie://`), "Download file", back; an always-visible **Player** topbar icon opens the current file in the local player; multi-file picker for packs (only completed files are listed).
247: - `playinfo` 404 → "No playable file yet" (or the waiting state above while the download runs).
248:

295: | `downloading`, `forcedDL` | `downloading` |

PROWLARR_BOOTSTRAP_INDEXERS=1

----COMPOSE----
name: movie-downloader

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: app
      POSTGRES_DB: moviedl
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U app -d moviedl"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 12
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [internal]

  qbittorrent:
    image: linuxserver/qbittorrent
    environment:
      PUID: "1000"
      PGID: "1000"
      TZ: Etc/UTC
      WEBUI_PORT: "8080"
    volumes:
      - qbconfig:/config
      - downloads:/downloads
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
      - "6881:6881"
      - "6881:6881/udp"
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [internal]

  prowlarr:
    image: linuxserver/prowlarr
    environment:
      PUID: "1000"
      PGID: "1000"
      TZ: Etc/UTC
      # Used by deploy/prowlarr-api-key.sh (mounted below) to pin the API key in
      # config.xml on every boot, so it can never drift from the backend's
      # PROWLARR_API_KEY when the prowlarr-config volume is recreated.
      PROWLARR_API_KEY: ${PROWLARR_API_KEY:?set PROWLARR_API_KEY in .env}
    volumes:
      - prowlarr-config:/config
      # linuxserver/prowlarr ignores PROWLARR__* env overrides; this init script
      # seeds/patches config.xml before Prowlarr starts.
      - ./deploy/prowlarr-api-key.sh:/custom-cont-init.d/99-prowlarr-api-key.sh:ro
    ports:
      - "9696:9696"
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [internal]

  flaresolverr:
    image: ghcr.io/flaresolverr/flaresolverr:latest
    environment:
      LOG_LEVEL: info
      TZ: Etc/UTC
    ports:
      - "8191:8191"
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [internal]

  backend:
    build: ./backend
    extra_hosts:
      # Some ISP/host DNS servers return a dead BunnyCDN edge for image.tmdb.org
      # (TCP times out). Pin a reachable edge; any BunnyCDN node serves the same images.
      - "image.tmdb.org:152.233.22.97"
    environment:
      TMDB_API_KEY: ${TMDB_API_KEY:?set TMDB_API_KEY in .env}
      OMDB_API_KEY: ${OMDB_API_KEY:-}
      PROWLARR_URL: http://prowlarr:9696
      PROWLARR_API_KEY: ${PROWLARR_API_KEY:?set PROWLARR_API_KEY in .env}
      QBITTORRENT_URL: http://qbittorrent:8080
      QBITTORRENT_USER: ${QBITTORRENT_USER:-admin}
      QBITTORRENT_PASS: ${QBITTORRENT_PASS:?set QBITTORRENT_PASS in .env}
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://app:app@postgres:5432/moviedl
      DOWNLOAD_DIR: /downloads
      PORT: "3000"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - downloads:/downloads
      - packages:/packages
      - art:/art
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [internal]

  frontend:
    build: ./frontend
    ports:
      - "5173:80"
    depends_on:
      - backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [internal]

volumes:
  pgdata:
  qbconfig:
  prowlarr-config:
  downloads:
  packages:
  art:

networks:
  internal:
    driver: bridge

# Credentials — what you need and where it goes

This file is a **template**. Never paste real secrets here — real values live only in `.env` (gitignored) and in the local-only `docs/credentials.local.md` (gitignored). If you accidentally commit a real key, rotate it immediately.

## Credentials checklist

| Service | What | Where to get it | `.env` variable |
|---------|------|-----------------|-----------------|
| TMDB | API key (v3) | themoviedb.org → Settings → API (free account) | `TMDB_API_KEY` |
| OMDb | API key (free) | omdbapi.com → API Key (mailed to you; ~1,000 req/day) | `OMDB_API_KEY` |
| Prowlarr | API key | Prowlarr UI → Settings → General → API Key (auto-generated) | `PROWLARR_API_KEY` |
| Prowlarr | Base URL | Compose-internal service name; only change if self-hosting elsewhere | `PROWLARR_URL` |
| qBittorrent | Web UI username | First qBittorrent Web UI login | `QBITTORRENT_USER` |
| qBittorrent | Web UI password | Set during first login — use a strong value (UI is LAN-exposed, D13) | `QBITTORRENT_PASS` |
| qBittorrent | Base URL | Compose-internal service name | `QBITTORRENT_URL` |
| PostgreSQL | `DATABASE_URL` | Self-contained in docker-compose (user `app`, no external account) | `DATABASE_URL` |
| Trackers (TPB, 1337x, …) | None — no keys | Configured in Prowlarr UI (Settings → Indexers), not in code | — |

Only external account required: **free TMDB API key**. Optionally add a **free OMDb key** (`OMDB_API_KEY`) so the wide Netflix-style tiles get real portrait posters; without it the tiles show a monogram.

## Boot order (Prowlarr chicken-and-egg)

1. `docker compose up -d prowlarr qbittorrent postgres`
2. Open Prowlarr UI → **Settings → Indexers → Add Indexer** → add at least one tracker (1337x, TPB, YTS, …). Test each one. The app is tracker-agnostic; without any enabled indexer the Sources list is empty.
3. If a public tracker fails its test with *"blocked by CloudFlare Protection"*, either pick a different one or run FlareSolverr:
   - `docker compose up -d flaresolverr`
   - Prowlarr UI → **Tools → FlareSolverr → Add** → URL `http://flaresolverr:8191` → set a **Tag** (e.g. `fs`) → Save.
   - On the blocked indexer, set the same **Tag**, then Test again.
4. Copy the Prowlarr API key (Settings → General) → paste into `.env` as `PROWLARR_API_KEY`.
5. Open qBittorrent Web UI once → set username/password → paste into `.env`.
6. Fill the remaining `.env` values, then `docker compose up -d --build`.

### Prowlarr API key vs indexers

Two separate things:
- **Indexers** (Settings → Indexers) — what Prowlarr searches to return sources.
- **API key** (Settings → General) — the auth value the backend sends as `X-Api-Key`.
  A missing/wrong key makes the Detail page show *"Prowlarr API key invalid — check PROWLARR_API_KEY"*;
  valid key but no indexers shows an empty Sources list.

## Security rules

- Never commit `.env`. It is gitignored.
- Never paste real keys into `docs/credentials.md` (committed). Use `docs/credentials.local.md` instead.
- The TMDB key must never reach the browser — images are proxied via `/api/images/tmdb/*`.
- qBittorrent and Prowlarr are published on your LAN (decision D13). qBittorrent has its own login; **Prowlarr has no auth** — keep it on a trusted network.
- If any key is ever leaked, rotate it (TMDB: revoke/regenerate in account settings; Prowlarr: regenerate API key).

display.text:
# Copy this file to .env and fill in real values. Never commit .env.
# See docs/credentials.md for where to get each value.

# TMDB — free API key, https://www.themoviedb.org -> Settings -> API
TMDB_API_KEY=your_tmdb_api_key

# OMDb — OPTIONAL free key, https://www.omdbapi.com -> your API key (email).
# Supplies the portrait poster each wide 16:9 card is composited from (D21).
# Leave empty to degrade to monogram tiles.
OMDB_API_KEY=

# Prowlarr — the prowlarr container pins this key into its config.xml on every
# boot (deploy/prowlarr-api-key.sh), so it always matches the backend.
# Optional: set 0 to disable automatic indexer creation on backend start.
# Optional: comma-separated names to auto-create (defaults below). 1337x is
# Cloudflare-protected and may fail unless Prowlarr can reach it.
PROWLARR_URL=http://prowlarr:9696
PROWLARR_API_KEY=your_prowlarr_api_key
PROWLARR_BOOTSTRAP_INDEXERS=1
PROWLARR_BOOTSTRAP_INDEXERS_LIST=YTS,LimeTorrents,TorrentDownload,1337x

# qBittorrent Web UI credentials (set on first login)
QBITTORRENT_URL=http://qbittorrent:8080
QBITTORRENT_USER=admin
QBITTORRENT_PASS=your_qbit_password

# PostgreSQL (self-contained in docker-compose; change locally if desired)
DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:app@postgres:5432/moviedl

# Shared downloads volume mount point (must match docker-compose.yml)
DOWNLOAD_DIR=/downloads

# Optional — local artwork cache volume for the poster-first tiles (D17). The
# backend downloads poster/background/logo files here once and serves them from
# /api/images/art/* (S8b). A named volume is mounted at /art by default.
ART_DIR=/art

# Backend HTTP port
PORT=3000

input.newString:
### 4.6 Portrait-poster pipeline (OMDb → local `art` volume) — D21, Downloads + Detail hero only
- Problem researched (D17/D21 history): no free API exposes *wide* per-title studio art except TMDB backdrops and FanArt.tv (Netflix's own title-card art is proprietary). D21 built the wide tile in-app from a legal portrait one-sheet and made it the rail-card art source; **T-002 supersedes that card use** (Home/Search rail cards now use the horizontal-poster/vertical-poster art of §4.7/D22). This pipeline now feeds only the **Downloads-page 2:3 row thumbnails** and the **Detail-hero blurred ground**.
- Portrait source = **OMDb** (Amazon-hosted, keyed by IMDb id).
- Config: optional `OMDB_API_KEY` in `.env`. Absent → those thumbnails/heroes show the monogram placeholder. Free tier is **1,000 requests/day**; `services/omdb.ts` enforces a conservative daily budget (~850) and treats a budget miss as a transient error, never as "no poster".
- Resolution chain (`lib/warmArt.ts` + image route, one time per title): TMDB `GET /{movie|tv}/{id}/external_ids` (`tmdb.imdbId`) → OMDb `GET /?apikey=…&i=tt…` → Amazon `Poster` URL → downloaded once to `ART_DIR` (`art_files`, kind `poster`) → served by **S8b**.
- Warm loop covers browse rails + downloads at boot and every `ART_WARM_INTERVAL_MS`; the S8b route additionally **warms on first miss**. Titles with no poster are recorded `empty` (7-day retry window) so OMDb is not re-asked.
- Enrichment: search/browse/detail/downloads payloads carry no `art` object (unchanged); DownloadsPage and the Detail hero render the portrait from `/api/images/art/:mediaType/:tmdbId/poster` directly and fall back to a monogram on 404/error.

### 4.7 Horizontal key-art + logo pipeline (fanart.tv + TMDB logos) — D22/T-002
- Problem: the default Home/Search card must read as a real **horizontal poster**, but no free API serves per-title *wide* one-sheets except fanart.tv's community "thumbnails" — landscape key-art **with the title baked in** (`moviethumb` for movies, `tvthumb` for TV — both 16:9). No real horizontal poster exists on OMDb/TMDB, so the fanart thumb is the deliberate wide-art source ("jerry-rig", per author).
- Config: optional `FANART_API_KEY` in `.env` (fanart.tv → login → API → Personal API Key). Absent → every card renders the fallback (backdrop + logo / typography). Requests go to `https://webservice.fanart.tv/v3/{movie|tv}/{tmdbId}?api_key=…`.
- Client (`services/fanart.ts`): `keyArt(mediaType, tmdbId)` → `{ status: "ok"|"empty"|"error", url }`. Picker `pickBestThumbUrl` ranks entries by (English first, then most `likes`). `404` → `empty` (storable); bad key/5xx/network → `error` (never stored as "no art").
- Cache: an `artCache` instance (`lib/artCache.ts`, generalized with a `kind` param — `poster`|`thumb`|`logo`) downloads each thumb once to `ART_DIR` under `art_files` kind `thumb`, file `{mediaType}_{tmdbId}_thumb.{ext}`; served by **S8c** `/api/images/fanart/:mediaType/:tmdbId/thumb` (warm-on-miss, immutable cache headers, empty rows cached 7 days). The fanart.tv key never reaches the browser.
- Logo cache: `TmdbClient.logoPath` (§4.1) → downloaded once to kind `logo`, file `{mediaType}_{tmdbId}_logo.{ext}` at `/original` size from `image.tmdb.org`; served by **S8b** `/api/images/art/:mediaType/:tmdbId/logo`. The transparent PNG is the CSS overlay on the backdrop in the horizontal fallback; coverage is patchy, so typography is the common final fallback.
- Card contract (frontend `TitleCard`): a **typography mark** (bold title + year over a bottom scrim; centered monogram+tile only when *no* art source exists) is always the base layer. Above it: TMDB backdrop → transparent logo → fanart thumb, each requested only when the tier below is actually needed. The hover pop-up (D20) still art prefers the backdrop, then the loaded key-art. The OMDb portrait composite is **never** used on Home/Search cards.

+### 4.6 Portrait-poster pipeline (OMDb → local `art` volume) — D21, Downloads + Detail hero only
+- Problem researched (D17/D21 history): no free API exposes *wide* per-title studio art except TMDB backdrops and FanArt.tv (Netflix's own title-card art is proprietary). D21 built the wide tile in-app from a legal portrait one-sheet and made it the rail-card art source; **T-002 supersedes that card use** (Home/Search rail cards now use the horizontal-poster/vertical-poster art of §4.7/D22). This pipeline now feeds only the **Downloads-page 2:3 row thumbnails** and the **Detail-hero blurred ground**.
+- Portrait source = **OMDb** (Amazon-hosted, keyed by IMDb id).
+- Config: optional `OMDB_API_KEY` in `.env`. Absent → those thumbnails/heroes show the monogram placeholder. Free tier is **1,000 requests/day**; `services/omdb.ts` enforces a conservative daily budget (~850) and treats a budget miss as a transient error, never as "no poster".
+- Resolution chain (`lib/warmArt.ts` + image route, one time per title): TMDB `GET /{movie|tv}/{id}/external_ids` (`tmdb.imdbId`) → OMDb `GET /?apikey=…&i=tt…` → Amazon `Poster` URL → downloaded once to `ART_DIR` (`art_files`, kind `poster`) → served by **S8b**.
+- Warm loop covers browse rails + downloads at boot and every `ART_WARM_INTERVAL_MS`; the S8b route additionally **warms on first miss**. Titles with no poster are recorded `empty` (7-day retry window) so OMDb is not re-asked.
+- Enrichment: search/browse/detail/downloads payloads carry no `art` object (unchanged); DownloadsPage and the Detail hero render the portrait from `/api/images/art/:mediaType/:tmdbId/poster` directly and fall back to a monogram on 404/error.
 
+### 4.7 Horizontal key-art + logo pipeline (fanart.tv + TMDB logos) — D22/T-002
+- Problem: the default Home/Search card must read as a real **horizontal poster**, but no free API serves per-title *wide* one-sheets except fanart.tv's community "thumbnails" — landscape key-art **with the title baked in** (`moviethumb` for movies, `tvthumb` for TV — both 16:9). No real horizontal poster exists on OMDb/TMDB, so the fanart thumb is the deliberate wide-art source ("jerry-rig", per author).
+- Config: optional `FANART_API_KEY` in `.env` (fanart.tv → login → API → Personal API Key). Absent → every card renders the fallback (backdrop + logo / typography). Requests go to `https://webservice.fanart.tv/v3/{movie|tv}/{tmdbId}?api_key=…`.
+- Client (`services/fanart.ts`): `keyArt(mediaType, tmdbId)` → `{ status: "ok"|"empty"|"error", url }`. Picker `pickBestThumbUrl` ranks entries by (English first, then most `likes`). `404` → `empty` (storable); bad key/5xx/network → `error` (never stored as "no art").
+- Cache: an `artCache` instance (`lib/artCache.ts`, generalized with a `kind` param — `poster`|`thumb`|`logo`) downloads each thumb once to `ART_DIR` under `art_files` kind `thumb`, file `{mediaType}_{tmdbId}_thumb.{ext}`; served by **S8c** `/api/images/fanart/:mediaType/:tmdbId/thumb` (warm-on-miss, immutable cache headers, empty rows cached 7 days). The fanart.tv key never reaches the browser.
+- Logo cache: `TmdbClient.logoPath` (§4.1) → downloaded once to kind `logo`, file `{mediaType}_{tmdbId}_logo.{ext}` at `/original` size from `image.tmdb.org`; served by **S8b** `/api/images/art/:mediaType/:tmdbId/logo`. The transparent PNG is the CSS overlay on the backdrop in the horizontal fallback; coverage is patchy, so typography is the common final fallback.
+- Card contract (frontend `TitleCard`): a **typography mark** (bold title + year over a bottom scrim; centered monogram+tile only when *no* art source exists) is always the base layer. Above it: TMDB backdrop → transparent logo → fanart thumb, each requested only when the tier below is actually needed. The hover pop-up (D20) still art prefers the backdrop, then the loaded key-art. The OMDb portrait composite is **never** used on Home/Search cards.
+
 ## 5. Canonical naming (single source of truth)
 | Term | Canonical name |
 |------|----------------|
 | TMDB media id | `tmdbId` |

 - TV seasons: from `GET /tv/{id}` map `seasons` to `TvSeasonSummary[]`, dropping `season_number === 0` and `episode_count <= 0` (S2). Episodes from `/tv/{id}/season/{n}` map `still_path` → `stillPath`, `runtime`, `air_date` → `airDate`.

Returns a `file_path` like `/abc123.png` or `null` (404/empty). The picked file is what the S8b `logo` cache downloads (`/original` size).
-- Images: `https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/{w500|w1280}/{path}` (proxied, S8).

 - Timeouts: 10s connect/read. Retries: 2, exponential backoff (0.5s, 1s).
 - Error mapping: non-2xx or network → throw `UpstreamError` → routes respond `502`.
 - Quirks: TV dates → `first_air_date`; movies → `release_date`. Normalize both to `year` (int) or null.

part.text:
T-002 is implemented and committed on `ticket/T-002` (`7d19fcd`). Not pushed, no PR, `.env`/`.opencode` untouched.

## What changed

**Part A — horizontal-poster rail cards (backend + frontend)**
- New `backend/src/services/fanart.ts` behind an interface: `FanartClient.keyArt()` resolves fanart.tv `moviethumb` (movie) / `tvthumb` (TV) — the TV field name was confirmed against live fanart.tv responses via public third-party consumers. Pure `pickBestThumbUrl` (English first, then most likes). `404` → `empty`, key/5xx/network → `error` (never cached as "no art").
- `lib/artCache.ts` generalized with a `kind` param (`poster`|`thumb`|`logo`); `ArtKind` union + schema check widened (idempotent `ALTER` adds `thumb`, keeps legacy kinds). New `fanartCache`/`logoCache` instances + optional `fanart` client wired in `index.ts`/`deps.ts` from optional `FANART_API_KEY`.
- Routes: **S8c** `/api/images/fanart/:mediaType/:tmdbId/thumb` (cached file, warm-on-miss, immutable headers, key never in the browser) and **S8b** extended to serve `logo` kind from TMDB `/images` logos (`TmdbClient.logoPath` + pure `pickBestLogoPath`). `.env.example`, `docker-compose.yml`, `docs/credentials.md` updated.
- `TitleCard` artwork stack (bottom→top): always-on **typography mark** → TMDB backdrop → transparent studio logo → fanart key-art, each tier requested only when needed, with a bounded retry budget. Total-art-missing keeps a centered monogram+title tile.

**Part B — vertical 2:3 mode**
- `store/posterStyleStore.ts` (zustand-persist, `localStorage movie-downloader:poster-style`, default Horizontal), applied as a `posters-vertical` class on the app shell; Settings gains a **Poster style** control.
